problems.device: planar solid-oxide fuel cell stack with ferritic-steel interconnect and LSCF cathode
problems.failure: chromium volatilized from the interconnect deposits at the cathode triple-phase boundary and raises polarization resistance, cutting power ~20% in 5000 h
problems.constraint: retrofit only: no change to interconnect alloy or cell footprint; power decay <5% over 10000 h at 750 C; any coating must stay conductive and adhere under thermal cycling
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: retrofit only: no change to interconnect alloy or cell footprint; power decay <5% over 10000 h at 750 C; any coating must stay conductive and adhere under thermal cycling
device of record: planar solid-oxide fuel cell stack with ferritic-steel interconnect and LSCF cathode
failure to address: interconnect-chromium-poisoning
